questions.question: Which of the following naturally occurring acids is present in ant stings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methanoic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The acid present in an ant sting is Formic acid.
 
• Formic acid (systematically called methanoic acid) is the simplest carboxylic acid.
 
• Molecular formula: HCOOH
 
• It is quite fatal for those ants as after stinging, their stinger is lost after which formic acid is forcibly released from their poison gland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Oxalic acid is an organic compound found in many plants. These include leafy greens, vegetables, fruits, cocoa, nuts, and seeds
 
• Lactic acid is a natural organic acid, found in milk and other food products such as meat and beer.
 
 
• It is used in the food industry as a preservative, flavor enhancer, and acid adjustment.
 
 
 
• Citric acid is found naturally in citrus fruits, like lemons and limes.
 
 
• It gives them their tart, sour taste.

questions.question: Why is there low population growth in a society that is underdeveloped and technologically backward?

options.text: Because both death rate and birth rate are high
Because both death rate and birth rate are low
Because such countries usually have strict government policies related to population growth
Because people migrate from underdeveloped countries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because both death rate and birth rate are high.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ​According to the **Theory of Demographic Transition,** the **First Stage** has a very **low population growth rate** because of **society's immature **and** outdated technology.**
 
• Growth rates are **low **as a result of the** high birth and death rates**, which result in a **small net growth rate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** third (and final) stage** is also characterized by **slow development** in a developed society, where the discrepancy between the** birth and death rates** has **decreased** significantly.
 
• A **transitional stage** from a** backward to an advanced stage** exists between these two stages.
 
• This stage is distinguished by extremely **rapid population expansion.**
 
• This** "population boom"** is brought about by the comparatively **swift reduction in mortality rates** brought about by **modern disease management techniques,** improved public health, and improved nutrition.

questions.question: Right to Education was added as a fundamental right in the Indian Constitution in______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Right to Education Act (RTE) provided free and compulsory education to children in 2009 and enforced it as a fundamental right under Article 21-A.
 
• The 86th amendment to the constitution of India in 2002, provided the Right to Education as a fundamental right in part III of the Constitution.
 
• The same amendment inserted Article 21A which made the Right to Education a fundamental right for children between 6-14 years.
 
• The 86th amendment provided for follow-up legislation for the Right to Education Bill 2008 and finally the Right to Education Act 2009.
 
• Originally Part IV of the Indian Constitution, Article 45 and Article 39 (f) of DPSP, had a provision for state-funded as well as equitable and accessible education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

86 Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Education in the Fundamental rights of the constitution.

 
• It made elementary education a fundamental right and added a new article 21A.
 
• It declares that the state shall provide compulsory education to all children of the age 6 to 14 years.
 
• It changed the subject of Article 45 in directive principles that state shall provide early childhood care and education for all children until they reach the age of 6 years.
 
• It also added a new fundamental duty in Article 51A that it is the duty of every citizen to provide opportunities for education to their children between the age of 6 to 14 years.
 
• This was amended in the year 2002.

questions.question: What is the coil of wire in the electric room heater known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Element**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** wire coil of a heater** is also sometimes referred to as the **heating element.**
 
• It is frequently constructed of** rare materials** like **platinum, tungsten, etc**.
 
• A heating element uses the J**oule heating process** to transform** electrical energy into heat.**
 
• Nowadays, a coil of wire is heated by an** electric current **and utilized to** produce and sustain high temperatures **throughout many** scientific procedures.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell:**

 
 
• A cell is a **solitary electrical energy source** that generates **current **through chemical reactions.
 
• "Electrical power supply" refers to an** electrical cell.**
 
 
 
• **Fuse:**
 
 
• A fuse is typically formed of a **current-conducting strip or wire **of readily** flammable metal.**
 
• It melts whenever the circuit it is part of is designed to carry a** current greater than **that for which the **fuse is intended, interrupting the circuit.**
 
 
 
• **Switch:**
 
 
• An electrical part called a switch is used to **turn electrical equipment on and off. **

questions.question: In which of the following sites of Indus Valley Civilisation was ‘The Great Bath’ found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjo-Daro.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Great Bath **was found in the **1920s** during **excavations at Mohenjo-Daro.**
 
• The Bath is **83 square meters** in size and was built with **beautiful masonr**y.
 
• The Big Bath is an ancient building in** Mohenjo-Daro **that dates to the **third millennium BCE.**
 
• It is said to have been used for** ceremonial bathing**.
 
• Mohenjo-Daro, popularly known as **"Mound of the Dead,**" was one of the greatest cities of the **ancient Indus Valley Civilization.**
 
• The majority of homes had **small bathrooms and mud-plastered walls**, and the streets had plenty of **drains and sanitary facilities,** indicating that the city was well-planned.
 
• **It was believed that Mohenjo-Daro was divided** into two sections:
 
 
• **Citadel, **which served as the site's ceremonial administrative centre, and 
 
• **Lower Town**, had courtyard houses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalibangan**:

 
 
• A significant provincial capital of the **Indus Valley Civilization **was Kalibangan.
 
• During excavations, an **Italian Indologist **found the **Kalibangan site.**
 
 
 
• **Dholavira:**
 
 
• **Gujarat's Bhachau Taluka of Kutch Distric**t is home to the archaeological site known as Dholavira.
 
• The city's most notable characteristic is that all of its structures are** made of stone**.
 
 
 
• **Lothal:**
 
 
• One of the most **southern Indus Valley civilization** sites was **Lothal**.
 
• It is located in the **Bhal region of the Indian state of Gujarat.**
 
• The discovery of numerous** Indus Valley Civilization** ruins in Lothal has made the city famous.
 
• Between **1955 and 1962, **Lothal underwent excavation.

questions.question: The oceanic crust of the earth mainly consists of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**silica and magnesium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Earth has three layers namely the crust, mantle and core.
 
• **Earth's crust is the earth's outermost layer and is divided into Oceanic crust and Continental crust**.
 
 
• **The crust comprises more than 90% of igneous and metamorphic rocks, and the rest with minerals, sandstones etc.**
 
 
 
• **The oceanic crust is mostly made up of basalt rocks** which are called volcanic rocks and are formed at oceanic ridges where tectonic plates are separated and is a thin and denser than the continental crust
 
 
• **This oceanic crust is referred to as "Sima" which means Silicon and Magnesium. Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• Silica or quartz is the most abundant material on earth's crust and is an oxide of silicon (Si).
 
• Magnesium (Mg) helps major organs like the Heart, bones and Muscles function smoothly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron is one of the most abundant metals on Earth and forms its Core. As an Alloy, Iron is used in manufacturing Steel, machinery, buildings etc.**
 
• Nickel (Ni) is a silvery white metal used in plating, and Nickel alloys in turbine blades and propeller shafts etc.
 
• Alumina or Aluminium oxide is a colourless crystalline substance used in abrasion resistant tiles and cutting tools.
 
• **The continental crust, the outermost layer of the earth's lithosphere forms a continental landmass, on the earth and is formed at the subduction zones.**
 
 
• Subduction zones are the place where tectonic plates converge.

questions.question: In which year was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1929.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Imperial Legislative Council** passed the** Child Marriage Restriction Act, of 1929,** on** September 28.**
 
• It set the legal marriage age for** men and women** at **18 and 14 r**espectively.
 
• It was changed to** 15 for females in 1949, **and then to **18 for girls and 21 for boys in 1978**, following India's independence.
 
• After its sponsor **Harbilas Sharda,** it is commonly referred to as the **Sarda Act.**
 
• On** 1 April 1930, six months **after it went into effect, it extended to all of British India.
 
• It came forth as a result of the **Indian social reform movement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021:**

 
 
• The **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**, is amended by the **bill to raise the legal age of consent** for **female marriage** from **18 to 21.**
 
• According to the 2006 Act, a person who was** married before reaching majority **may request an annulment within two years** (i.e., before 20 years of age).**
 
• This is extended by the Bill to** five years (i.e., 23 years of age).**

questions.question: In which season are Kharif crops grown?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **Monsoon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The** monsoon season** on the Indian subcontinent begins with the** Kharif agricultural season**.
 
• Typically, Kharif crops are sown at the **start of the first monsoon rains.**
 
• From the **third week of September to October,** the harvesting season starts.
 
• **Paddy, maize, bajra, jowar, soybean, castor, cotton, sugarcane, turmeric, chilly, bitter gourd, guar, okra, brinjal, turmeric, and ragi **are some examples of Kharif crops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi crops** are those that are raised **throughout the winter months.**
 
• They are sown between** October and November**, and they are harvested between **April and June.**
 
• **Wheat, barley, peas, grams, and mustard** are a few of the important rabi crops.
 
• **Wheat **is the** main rabi crop **in India and is produced in vast quantities.

questions.question: What is the longitudinal valley lying between lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dun**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Himalayas are a part of the northern plain that spread from Kashmir to Arunachal Pradesh for over 2500 km which are formed by tectonic plate collision between the Eurasian plate and the Indian plate.**
 
• They are divided into Greater Himalayas, Trans-Himalayas (or called the Tibetan Himalayan range), Shivaliks and Lesser Himalayas.
 
• **Duns are narrow-shaped longitudinal valleys located between the lesser Himalayas and the Shivaliks. Hence option 4 is correct.**
 
• **Shivaliks lie southernmost tip of the Himalayas and are called the Outer Himalayas** and run parallel to the lesser Himalayas from Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
 
• **They are also called Churia Hills and flow from the Indus to Brahmaputra Rivers.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kangra is a district in Himachal Pradesh** and has India's one of the oldest fort named Kangra fort.
 
• **Sind is the third-largest province in Pakistan** bordered by Balochistan and Punjab.
 
• **The TRANS ****Himalayas includes the Karakoram range, Zaskar range, Kailash range etc. **
 
• Trans Himalayas separates India from the Tibetan Plateau and has the world's highest peaks including Mt. Everest.
 
• **The Greater Himalayas are called Himadri and is the highest mountain range in the Himalayas** and including Kangchenjunga, the third highest mountain in the world and Gangotri glacier.

__
 
• Classical dance forms in India include Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Mohiniyattam etc.
 
• **Odissi is a classical dance from the Odisha** state which follows Natya Sastra principles.

• Madhavi Mudgal is a classical dancer in Odissi, but she also learnt Bharatnatyam and Kathak.

• **Manipuri is a classical dance from Manipur** state and is based on Vaishnavism, Shaktism and Shaivism.

 
 
• Raas, Nata Sankirtan, Dhola Cholam etc are the types of Manipuri dance styles.
 
 
 
• **Lai Haraoba is the earliest dance in Manipur and is the oldest festival celebrated there.**
 
• Guru Bipin Sinha and Darshana Jhaveri are among the famous Manipuri dancers.
 
• **Kathak is one of the major classical dance form that has roots in the north India and it has its origin in the Uttar Pradesh state.**
 
• Rohini Bhate, Sitara Devi, Sunder Prasad are some of the famous Kathak dancers.
 
• **Sattriya dance form is originated in Assam** and was introduced by Mahapurusha Sankaradeva, a vaishnavaite from Assam.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first solar project to break the grid parity barrier in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rewa Ultra Mega Solar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Grid parity is a time at which the electricity cost from the alternative source energy (such as PV or solar) cost is less than or equal to the electrical grid.**
 
• When the power generation is more than 500 MW, then it is called an ultra mega solar park.
 
• **Rewa solar project, set up in Madhya Pradesh becomes the first solar project to break the grid parity barrier in India. Hence option 3 is correct.**
 
 
• ​It is a 750 MW (three units generating 250 MW each) project which was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2020.
 
• **This project is estimated to reduce carbon dioxide emissions to 15 lakh tons per year.**
 
 
 
• It was developed by Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Ltd and Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park in Andhra Pradesh is the world's largest single location operational solar energy park with 1000 MW (250 MW power from each panel) power generation.**

 
 
• ​It was inaugurated by then Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu in Jan 2019.
 
 
 
• **Bhadla Solar Park located in Rajasthan is the world's largest solar park which has a capacity of 2.2 GW or 2240 MW.**
 
 
• ​It was commissioned in 2017 and has more than 10 mn solar panels.
 
 
 
• **Charanka Solar Park located in Gujarat generates around 600 MW** and was inaugurated n 2012 by then Chief Minister of Gujarat Narendra Modi.

• Grammy awards are presented for outstanding achievement in the music field and are presented by the Recording Academy in the United States which were earlier called the Gramophone awards.
 
 
• **The Grammy awards were first presented in 1958-59 and have been held annually.**
 
 
 
• AR Rahman is an Indian music composer who works in many languages like Tamil, Hindi, Telugu etc and also in Hollywood with 20th Century fox studios.

questions.question: As per the Constitution of India, every Legislative Assembly of every State, unless sooner dissolved, shall continue for _____ from the date appointed for its first meeting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• State Legislative Assembly​

 
 
• It is a Legislative body of the state.
 
• Subject to the provisions of Article 333, the Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of not more than five hundred, and not less than sixty, members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the State.
 
• Each State shall be divided into territorial constituencies.
 
• Members of the State Legislative Assembly, are elected directly by voting, from a set of candidates who stands in their respective constituencies.
 
 
 
• **​A Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) is a representative, elected by the voters of an electoral district (constituency) to the legislature of the State government in the Indian system of government.**
 
 
• From each constituency, the people elect one representative who then becomes a member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA). 
 
 
 
• Lok Sabha
 
 
• It is the lower house of the Indian Parliament.
 
• It is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 552.
 
• 25 years is the minimum age for holding office in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The term of the members of Lok Sabha is a maximum of 5 years.
 
• Motions of no confidence against the government can be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
